mode: static file parsing only, the specimen is never loaded or executed

confidence_scale.HIGH: an instruction, an immediate or a directory entry settles it
confidence_scale.MEDIUM: derived from the file but conditional on one run time property
confidence_scale.LOW: the mechanism is known, the deciding instance data is absent from the file
confidence_scale.OPEN: not decidable from the file alone, carried as an open question

status_vocabulary.OBSERVED: the structure is present and settled by an instruction or an immediate
status_vocabulary.ABSENT: the structure is proven not to exist inside the audited range
status_vocabulary.ASYMMETRIC: the two halves of a cross function pair sit in different functions
status_vocabulary.UNRESOLVED: the file does not decide the question

function.name: rip_redirect
function.role: moves a suspended thread from a recorded original address to the matching position in a rebuilt image
function.signature: void f(LONG record_index_or_minus_one, THREADIDLIST* out), windows x64, out block in rcx, index in edx
function.return_value: none, the caller discards the return register at both call sites

rva32_literal_classification.note: the literal is the rip relative displacement of the instruction that precedes it, and it resolves to a different address

enumeration.arguments: snapshot handle, THREADENTRY32 at rsp+0x30 with dwSize 0x1C
snapshot handle, dwSize re-armed to 0x1C before the call

selection.use: th32OwnerProcessID at structure offset 0xC must equal the result
th32ThreadID at structure offset 0x8 must differ from the result

thread_lifecycle.arguments: dwDesiredAccess=0x5A, bInheritHandle=FALSE, dwThreadId from the array
the snapshot handle, then one handle per opened thread

resume_absent_in_subject.note: the subject suspends and never resumes, the orchestrator owns the resume

thread_handles.alive_during: the enumeration only, the handle is closed before any thread is opened

thread_handles.stored_in: rbx, the same register the snapshot handle used
close_paths: the start index is at or above the limit
the record scan ran to the exclusive limit

thread_handles.obtain_expr: OpenThread(0x5A, FALSE, out.array[i]) in the caller
thread_handles.note: a second, independent handle per identifier, so the resume does not depend on the handle the subject used

out_block.expression: the caller's frame block, passed in rcx; the orchestrator passes its own rsp+0x28 on both call paths
out_block.zeroing_width: one 128 bit store covers the pointer, the capacity and the count

element.value: a thread identifier read at structure offset 0x8

capacity_model.growth: doubling, the new byte count is capacity times two times the element size

element.bounds_evidence: 0x1E187 compares the count with the capacity before every append

context_buffer.frame_fit_note: the structure starts at the frame offset above and ends exactly where the stack cookie is stored, so the frame is sized for one structure plus the cookie

context_flags.note: the low bit is the control selector of the CONTEXT group, the value is the control group request

rip.note: the frame copy is updated before the apply, so the next record reads the value the previous record intended to install

context_buffer.fields_not_touched: every other field of the structure, including the whole general purpose register group

aliasing.shared_slot: the thread entry structure and the context structure occupy the same frame slot
aliasing.note: the enumeration loop closes the snapshot handle before the thread loop opens the first context, so the two uses never interleave

fields_read_by_subject.name: anchor
fields_read_by_subject.role: the address the 0x28 list offsets are added to

fields_read_by_subject.name: image_base
fields_read_by_subject.role: the base of the rebuilt image the 0x30 list offsets are added to

fields_read_by_subject.name: flags
fields_read_by_subject.role: the skip bit hides the record from the rewrite

fields_read_by_subject.name: entry_count
fields_read_by_subject.role: the number of parallel list entries, low nibble only

fields_read_by_subject.name: match_list
fields_read_by_subject.meaning: rec[0x28][i], byte built as the instruction start offset from rec + 0x00

fields_read_by_subject.name: target_list
fields_read_by_subject.meaning: rec[0x30][i], byte built as the window cursor past that instruction

flag_interaction.ordering: the flag is written by the inline patcher, which the orchestrator runs after the redirect on both paths
flag_interaction.consequence: a record is visible to the rewrite only on a pass that happens before the patcher has processed it

rip_reconstruction.comparison: exact 64 bit equality, the branch on inequality advances the entry cursor
rip_reconstruction.parallel_lists: one entry cursor drives both byte loads, so entry i of 0x28 pairs with entry i of 0x30

per_entry_semantics.match_byte: the offset of an instruction start from the record anchor
per_entry_semantics.target_byte: the window cursor just past that instruction
per_entry_semantics.reading: a suspended thread is redirected only when its instruction pointer sits exactly on a recorded instruction start
per_entry_semantics.landing: the replacement is the same relative position in the rebuilt image, past the instruction that was about to run

window.consequence: both list bytes stay representable in one unsigned byte, so the byte lists cannot wrap

rip_reconstruction.applies_per_thread: at most the number of scanned records, because the cursor chain continues after an apply
rip_reconstruction.chaining: the frame copy of the instruction pointer is rewritten before the apply, so the next record matches against the replacement value
inert_conditions: the skip bit 0x2 is set on the record
the low nibble of rec + 0x24 is zero
the start index is at or above the exclusive limit

caller_lock.contended_path: 0x1E38F sleeps and retries, so the subject runs at most once concurrently
caller_lock.note: the subject reads the record table and the record count without any lock of its own, which is sound only because both call sites sit inside the held region

heap_gate.effect: an unpublished heap handle makes the orchestrator return 2 before any call site

record_availability.skip_effect: the bulk path needs one record without the bit, the single path refuses a record that has it

thread_availability.source: the toolhelp snapshot, so a thread that does not exist at enumeration time is never redirected

the caller frees the identifier array and releases the once flag

consistency.rule: the requested access must cover every operation the sequence performs
consistency.evidence: 0x5A decomposes into the suspend, get context, set context and query information rights, one per operation used

consistency.rule: only three argument registers are set before the open call
consistency.evidence: the open entry point takes three parameters, so the untouched fourth register is not a missing argument

consistency.rule: the frame must hold the structure the code fills
consistency.evidence: the structure at offset 0x30 of size 0x4D0 ends exactly at the cookie offset 0x500

consistency.rule: the two touched fields must belong to the requested group
consistency.evidence: ContextFlags at structure offset 0x30 and Rip at 0xF8 are both control group fields, and the request mask selects the control group
one suspend per opened thread in the subject, one resume per collected identifier in the caller, so a pre-existing suspend count is preserved

consistency.rule: the append must not pass the capacity
consistency.evidence: 0x1E187 compares the count with the capacity and grows first, so the count never exceeds the capacity
the subject allocates and the caller frees, both on the same heap global, and every path that published the array reaches the free

consistency.rule: the two lists must fit inside the record stride
consistency.evidence: the builder refuses a ninth entry and the two lists own 0x10 bytes of the 0x38 byte stride

consistency.rule: the count read must not lose entries the builder produced
consistency.evidence: the builder caps the count at eight and the reader masks with 0xF, which is wider than the cap

consistency.rule: both list values must stay representable in one byte
consistency.evidence: the window is capped at 0x32 bytes, so neither the start offset nor the cursor past an instruction can exceed a byte

consistency.rule: the thread must leave the original address before the bytes there change
the flag must not hide a record before its own rewrite
consistency.evidence: the flag write at 0x1E336 runs after the redirect on both paths, so the skip bit is clear while the rewrite is decided

consistency.rule: one register must not hold two live handles
consistency.evidence: the snapshot handle is closed at the enumeration exit, which is before the first thread open, so the reuse of rbx is safe

consistency.rule: the enumeration structure and the context must not be live at the same time
consistency.evidence: the enumeration loop completes and the snapshot handle is closed before the thread loop reaches the first context use

consistency.rule: a table that can grow must be reloaded
consistency.evidence: 0x1E21A reloads the array pointer after every applied context

negative_findings.statement: KERNEL32.dll!ResumeThread is not referenced between the first and the last byte of the subject
negative_findings.evidence: the resume import slot is referenced only from the orchestrator
negative_findings.consequence: every thread this function suspends is left suspended when it returns, and only the two known callers undo it

negative_findings.statement: the subject has no return value and no output flag that reports whether a redirect happened
negative_findings.evidence: both call sites overwrite the return register with an unrelated load immediately after the call
negative_findings.consequence: the orchestrator cannot distinguish a completed rewrite from a skipped thread

negative_findings.statement: no general purpose register is read from or written to the context
negative_findings.evidence: the request mask selects the control group and only the instruction pointer is touched
negative_findings.consequence: the redirected thread continues with the register state of the old location, which is only sound when the replacement is a fresh entry

negative_findings.statement: the subject writes no executable bytes and requests no page protection change
negative_findings.evidence: no protection or cache flush import is referenced in the range, the only writes are into the frame copy and the out block
negative_findings.consequence: the mechanism is a control flow relocation only, the byte level patching is a separate function

negative_findings.statement: the subject is not address taken and has no thunk or function pointer referring to it
negative_findings.evidence: no absolute pointer literal, no rip relative reference and only the two direct call sites
negative_findings.consequence: the two audited call sites are the complete caller set for this build of the specimen

negative_findings.statement: the record image base field is never tested on its own
negative_findings.evidence: only the sum with the target byte is compared against zero
negative_findings.consequence: a null image base with a non zero target byte would pass the gate and install a very small instruction pointer

unresolved.question: what invokes the orchestrator, and therefore what activates the whole mechanism
unresolved.reason: the file contains no direct call site, no rip relative reference and no pointer literal for the orchestrator

unresolved.question: which records exist at run time, and which module and export each anchor belongs to
unresolved.reason: the table slot is zero filled in the file and the registrar is only reachable from the builder, so no record can be enumerated statically

unresolved.question: can the record image base field be published as zero
unresolved.reason: the field is written by the registrar from an arena block, and whether a null block can reach that store is not settled by the record layout alone

unresolved.question: how often a suspended thread is actually at one of the recorded instruction starts
unresolved.reason: the mechanism depends on the run time instruction pointer landing on a recorded offset, and no scheduling or timing data exists in the file
